articleTitle: Ring cameras go mobile as Amazon debuts AI-powered security drone and robot
summary: Amazon announced Ring Drone Cam and Ring Rover Cam, mobile security cameras using AI Pilot, onboard sensors and cloud processing to map indoor spaces, navigate obstacles and investigate alerts. Scheduled shipments begin December 16, 2026, for the Rover and January 27, 2027, for the drone, subject to FCC authorization for the drone, while privacy concerns center on indoor surveillance, cloud access and Ring’s history of security failures.

deviceA.name: Ring Drone Cam
specs: Flying indoor security camera using AI Pilot, device cameras, specialized vision models, on-device sensors and cloud processing.
Initial mapping requires the customer to carry the drone through indoor spaces; AI Pilot identifies rooms and suggests patrol points.
148-degree field of view, 360-degree rotation and 2K video.
Two LED lights activate in low-light conditions.
8 minutes of flight time on a new, fully-charged battery under controlled conditions; charging dock included.
Scheduled routes require an Amazon Ring Protect plan.
Can automatically investigate notifications from connected Ring cameras, sensors or alarms by flying preset routes.
Direct control through Alexa Home Map.
Navigation may degrade around reflective surfaces such as polished marble or wet tile, featureless matte walls, frameless glass and mirrors.
Amazon says recordings will use Throw Away the Key Encryption; recording indicators are provided.
deviceA.price: $250 as reported in the article; $249.99 in Amazon’s announcement.
deviceA.availability: January 27, 2027, subject to FCC authorization; customers can register for email updates.

deviceB.name: Ring Rover Cam
specs: Wheeled indoor security robot designed for business and inspired by customer feedback about Amazon Astro.
AI Pilot maps spaces through autonomous exploration and uses cameras, vision models, on-device sensors and cloud processing.
Livestreams and records in up to 4K, including while patrolling; performs a 360-degree scan at designated locations.
Doorbell-ring, motion-event and Live View recordings are stored in the cloud for up to 180 days.
Automatically responds to connected Ring device alerts by visiting programmed patrol points.
Limited to a single-floor, indoor environment; cannot climb stairs.
Incompatible with curved edges, sunken areas, flooring transitions greater than 1.375 inches (3.5 centimeters), and black glossy floors.
Automatically adjustable camera mast provides views over counters, shelving and obstacles.
Advertised coverage of up to 5,000 square feet (465 square meters).
Siren, light tower and microphone for two-way audio.
Amazon says recordings will use Throw Away the Key Encryption; LED indicators and screen notifications disclose recording activity.
deviceB.price: $1,000 as reported in the article; $999.99 in Amazon’s announcement.
deviceB.availability: Available for preorder, with shipping scheduled for December 16, 2026.

coreControversy.corporateClaim: Amazon presents autonomous mobile cameras as a way to investigate disturbances and monitor spaces beyond fixed-camera coverage while offering privacy and security without compromise through recording indicators and Throw Away the Key Encryption.
coreControversy.criticismOrAlarm: EFF describes the encryption as an improvement over Ring’s former defaults but short of end-to-end encryption, and criticizes features allowing law enforcement to request footage or live-stream access. Ryan Calo previously warned that flying indoor cameras create additional opportunities to surveil others and expose sensitive or identifying details of homes and businesses.
coreControversy.regulatoryOrHistoricalPrecedent: Ring Drone Cam requires FCC authorization before sale. Always Home Cam was temporarily sold by invitation in September 2021 as a Day 1 Edition product. A 2023 FTC investigation charged Ring with allowing employees and contractors to watch private recordings and described security failures enabling hackers to access 55,000 US customers’ accounts. Familiar Faces, available on fixed doorbell cameras starting in December 2025, is the subject of a class action lawsuit.

hiddenCatchesAndLimits: AI Pilot relies partly on cloud processing rather than operating entirely on-device; setup produces a digital floor plan of the customer’s indoor spaces.
The drone’s scheduled patrol functionality requires an Amazon Ring Protect subscription, beyond the hardware purchase.
The drone’s January 27, 2027, shipping target depends on FCC authorization; the announcement states that it cannot be offered for sale or lease until authorization is obtained.
The drone’s 8 minutes of flight time is qualified by a new, fully-charged battery and controlled conditions, not an unconditional operating guarantee.
Reflective surfaces, featureless matte walls, frameless glass and mirrors may degrade drone navigation.

Rover coverage of up to 5,000 square feet (465 square meters) does not overcome its single-floor restriction or incompatibility with curved edges, sunken areas, flooring transitions greater than 1.375 inches (3.5 centimeters), and black glossy floors.
Rover event videos may remain in the cloud for up to 180 days.
Throw Away the Key Encryption is not end-to-end encryption: Ring’s cloud AI features can temporarily access video encryption keys before those keys are deleted.
Recording indicators disclose activity but do not resolve concerns about surveillance of other people indoors or access to sensitive details of private spaces.
Facial recognition is not announced for the new robots; the existing Familiar Faces feature on fixed Ring doorbells should not be attributed to them.
Calo’s warnings concerned the earlier flying-camera initiative, while the Familiar Faces class action concerns the fixed-camera feature.

avoidAdvice: Do not treat the drone as continuously airborne security: its stated flight time is 8 minutes under specified conditions.
Do not assume the Rover can cover multiple floors or navigate all indoor flooring configurations.
Do not equate recording indicators or Throw Away the Key Encryption with end-to-end confidentiality.
Do not treat the drone’s planned release as unconditional before FCC authorization.
fitAdvice: The products extend Ring monitoring from fixed viewpoints to mobile indoor patrols and automated alert investigation.
The drone offers 2K video with a 148-degree field of view and 360-degree rotation; the Rover offers up to 4K video, an adjustable mast and two-way audio.
Deployment decisions must account for cloud processing, subscription-dependent scheduling, navigation restrictions and the privacy of people recorded inside homes or workplaces.
Advertised navigation, coverage and endurance capabilities remain manufacturer claims rather than independently tested performance findings.
